slides.headline: YOUR NAME IS LEAKING 39 PROFILES TO STRANGERS. THESE 7 STEPS KILL THEM ALL.
slides.image_prompt: Bare forearm from right, one finger jabbing glowing central icon on clean background; 39 electric-blue circles with connections; electric-blue against warm amber accents; documentary news photo, harsh flash; personal data violation emotion, not generic surveillance.

slides.headline: 1) SEARCH YOUR OWN NAME LIKE A STRANGER WOULD
slides.body: He searched his real name and old emails on Google. He found 39 profiles he had completely forgotten existed. You are probably exposed three or four searches deeper than you think.

slides.headline: 2) PULL EVERY OLD USERNAME YOU EVER USED
slides.body: A gaming username from 2016 can still connect Reddit, GitHub, and old forums back to your real name. Your oldest usernames are the most dangerous, because you forgot what you posted under them.

slides.headline: 3) SORT EVERY DEAD ACCOUNT INTO 3 BUCKETS
slides.body: A post from 2014 is still there for anyone who knows where to look. Even profiles you cannot delete still have personal details you can strip out.

slides.headline: 6 DETAILS. YOUR WHOLE LIFE EXPOSED.
slides.body:
Anyone who finds all six can locate, impersonate, and access your accounts.

"For each profile I paste, find every public mention of my city, birthday, workplace, and email. Tell me which ones to delete."

slides.headline: 5) PUSH THE BAD RESULTS OFF PAGE ONE
slides.body: He buried 5 public mentions by outranking them with updated profiles on sites Google already trusts. Some of those old sites still have your login sitting open.

slides.headline: 6) CLOSE EVERY LOGIN YOUR EMAIL REMEMBERS
slides.body: He found 16 logins still active: • Job boards • Forums • Tools he had completely forgotten about Closing those logins is not enough if the accounts you kept are still wide open.

slides.headline: 7) LOCK DOWN EVERY ACCOUNT THAT'S LEFT
slides.body: Four hours. 39 profiles found. 16 logins closed. 5 mentions buried. "Do a final security pass: review my privacy settings, connected apps, and enable two-factor authentication on every account."

slides.headline: SAVE THIS: 7 STEPS TO SCRUB YOUR ONLINE IDENTITY
slides.body:
Search your name like a stranger
Map every old username
Delete your city, job, and birthday
Close every login your email remembers
Lock down accounts with 2FA

Daily AI news + real skills

caption:
Swipe through all 7 steps. ChatGPT spent 4 hours cleaning one person's online identity and found 39 profiles they forgot existed. 🔍

Step 1: search your full name and old emails to build an exposure map, Step 2: pull every old username and run it by platform type, Step 3: open each dead account and sort into delete, private, or update, Step 4: remove every public mention of your city, job, birthday, and old email, Step 5: update your strongest profiles to outrank bad results you cannot delete, Step 6: search your inbox for welcome and verify to find forgotten logins, Step 7: enable 2FA and remove linked apps from every account you are keeping.

Most people have never audited their digital footprint. One name search reveals old accounts and profiles from platforms you thought you left years ago. Your identity is managed by you or by whoever finds it first. Running a business? DM us "AI" and we will show you what this could do for yours.

Sources: Numan_Ai12

hook_sharpen.why: [1] hits harder because 'YOUR NAME IS LEAKING' creates immediate personal threat and urgency that makes you swipe. [2] promises a solution but reads like generic listicle advice so you might scroll past.
